correctness.rationale: Each agent has a uniform latent matched-partner priority x_u∈[0,1] within the top indifference class. Conditional on all x, distinct unmatched reciprocal top-tie edges block independently with probability x_u x_v, yielding the exact graph integral ∫∏_edges(1-x_u x_v) and its finite edge-subset expansion. Tree elimination retains affine messages A−Bx; multiplying and integrating a degree-d child polynomial costs O(d²), summed to O(s²) rational operations with polynomial bit lengths. On paths and cycles, the rank-two kernel Kf(x)=∫_0^1(1-xy)f(y)dy has eigenvalues (2±√7)/6, giving the stated path recurrence and c_j eigenvalue power sum. The source verifier code was read, and independent exact fraction checks tested all 63 bipartite forests from three matching pairs plus the six-cycle factor 5027/23328. The general forest result relies on the induction, not a finite census.
residual_risks: No polynomial exact algorithm is claimed for general reciprocal top-tie graphs.
The independence assumption requires agents independently refining top ties; correlated tie breaking invalidates edge factorization.

Aziz et al Theorem 8 gives tractability when one side is certain, a different hypothesis. value.rationale: Stability probability of a fixed matching is a natural uncertainty measure. Sparse reciprocal competition trees provide a mathematically motivated tractability island within a generally hard exact-counting problem; path/cycle formulas yield precise explicit exponential rates. The result makes no arbitrary-graph algorithm claim.
residual_risks: Sparse reciprocal top-tie graphs are restrictive; tie-breaking correlation or strong preferences above partners fall outside scope.
